prompt: A JUDO application's REST update call answers HTTP 500 and the log says 'Outdated instance to update'. Explain why it happens, what status and code the client gets, how a custom service should retry the update, and whether the generated admin UI protects two users editing the same record.
check: optimistic locking via __version: the check runs only when the update payload contains __version
the REST answer is HTTP 500 with code INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (not a business/409 status), detected by the message
retry: read the entity again, apply the changes to the fresh copy, update again
the generated UI client copies __version only when it is a string / does not send it, so UI edits are not protected unless __version is sent explicitly

prompt: I want a public page in a JUDO app that lists products without login, plus a button to log in as a customer. Which actor settings matter (and their defaults), how is the guest landing page provided in the frontend, and what build problem can adding a third actor cause and how do I avoid it?
check: an effectively anonymous actor: anonymous=true and no mapped principal; it gets no realm and calls need no token
anonymous defaults to true in the metamodel, so authenticated actors need anonymous=false
supportGuestAccess applies only to a non-anonymous actor; the guest page is a registered GuestPage service / default shows Login button
a third actor can produce duplicate type imports that break pnpm format (biome); cause is actor order in the ESM->UI transformation; workaround: create the new actor first and check generated imports

prompt: I need a nightly job in a JUDO application that writes data, plus an interceptor that records an audit row on every product update without breaking the update. How do I schedule the job, what happens to the transaction if the audit write fails and I catch the exception, and what must I add so integration tests can use a library the app module declares with provided scope?
check: no platform scheduler / no Quartz feature in Karaf: the application bundles Quartz itself
on PostgreSQL a caught DAO failure aborts the whole transaction; let it propagate or move the write to an async interceptor
provided-scope dependencies of the app module are not on the integration-test class path; declare them in the integration-test module too (NoClassDefFoundError otherwise)

prompt: In a JUDO project I must rename an entity attribute without losing data, add a new required column that existing rows must get a value for, and apply the change to a persistent PostgreSQL database during local development. What is the safe procedure and which commands or files are involved?
check: rename with the CLI (update <fqn> --set name=...) keeps the xmi:id, so the incremental Liquibase diff emits renameColumn and data survives
a backfill for existing rows needs a hand-written data changeset (UPDATE ... WHERE ... IS NULL) in the migration folder
./judo.sh schema-upgrade applies the difference to the running persistent PostgreSQL database (schema_dir setting)
